note: REGRESSION GUARD for the duplicate-key rule (SPEC.md 4.1 'No duplicate keys' + 8 step 2). Top-level "spec_version" is repeated: the first occurrence (visually, at the top of the file) is the supported scpe/0.1; a duplicate "spec_version": "scpe/9.9" is appended as the manifest's LAST top-level key. Before that rule existed this vector returned unsupported-version in all three implementations: their JSON libraries share a last-wins convention, so each resolved the duplicate to scpe/9.9 and rejected THAT as an unsupported MAJOR. Right refusal, wrong reason -- it worked only because the duplicated key happened to be spec_version. A duplicated contributor, subject, or attestations would have been resolved just as silently on the way to a verdict, and a fourth implementation whose parser is first-wins or error-on-duplicate (RFC 8259 permits all three) would have read these exact signed bytes as a different document. The rule closes that: a duplicate key at any nesting depth is a step-2 parse rejection, folded into signature-invalid like every other unreadable manifest -- the same label imprecision documented in utf8-bom-manifest, since the SSHSIG over these bytes may well be intact and the status enum has no separate malformed-manifest value; the real cause is reported in `detail`, where all three share the shape 'manifest unparsable: duplicate JSON key ...' and differ only in how each language quotes the key name. This vector now guards the rule rather than flagging its absence: if an implementation stops rejecting duplicates, the status falls back to unsupported-version here, and for a duplicate of any other key it would slip past this check entirely. STATUS SOURCE: unlike every other expected.json in this directory, this value has NOT been copied from a verifier run -- it is read off the three implementations of the rule (verify_envelope.py's `_no_duplicate_keys` object_pairs_hook, verify.go's token walk, scpe.rs's map visitor), each rejecting at step 2 through the pre-existing 'manifest unparsable' branch. Re-run verify_all.py plus the Go and Rust binaries and correct this file if any of the three disagrees.
